title: Extrinsic orbital Edelstein effect from asymmetric scattering
authors: Sankar Sarkar, Koushik Ghorai, Amit Agarwal
abstract: The generation and manipulation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) by an external electric field constitute one of the central themes of orbitronics. In particular, the electrically induced nonequilibrium OAM polarization, known as the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE), has attracted considerable attention in recent years. While the intrinsic band-geometric mechanism and the role of conventional symmetric impurity scattering in the OEE are well understood, the contribution from disorder-induced asymmetric scattering remains unclear. Here, we develop a semiclassical theory that separates the OEE into intrinsic, Drude, side-jump, and third- and fourth-order skew-scattering channels. Unlike the Drude channel, the intrinsic, side-jump, and skew-scattering responses survive only in systems with broken time-reversal symmetry. We find that in a magnetized Rashba two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG), these disorder-induced mechanisms can substantially exceed the intrinsic contribution. Remarkably, we find that for a system with Rashba coupling of $1$ $eV Å$, the orbital magnetization is about one order of magnitude larger than the spin magnetization for the chosen parameters, highlighting the crucial role of orbital degrees of freedom in the Edelstein effect.
summary: This theoretical work develops a detailed semiclassical theory to analyze the Orbital Edelstein Effect (OEE) in a Rashba 2DEG, specifically addressing the role of disorder. The key finding is that disorder-induced asymmetric scattering channels (side-jump and skew-scattering) can dominate the orbital magnetization, highlighting the crucial role of orbital degrees of freedom over spin degrees of freedom in this effect.
main_problem: The paper investigates the previously unclear contribution of disorder-induced asymmetric scattering mechanisms to the Orbital Edelstein Effect (OEE). It aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical decomposition of the total OEE.
main_result: The disorder-induced side-jump and skew-scattering mechanisms can significantly enhance the orbital magnetization, potentially exceeding the intrinsic contribution by an order of magnitude in a magnetized Rashba 2DEG.
method: The authors developed a semiclassical Boltzmann theory, decomposing the total OAM polarization into five distinct channels corresponding to different scattering mechanisms (intrinsic, Drude, side-jump, and two skew-scattering orders).
model_or_system: The minimal model used is a magnetized Rashba two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) subjected to an external electric field and impurity disorder potential. The analysis is performed using the semiclassical Boltzmann equation.
key_observables:
Orbital magnetization ($\delta L_
u$), Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) polarization, and the susceptibility tensors quantifying the response in each scattering channel.
important_parameters: Rashba coupling strength (SOC), magnetic field strength, and the scattering rates derived from the impurity potential.
main_assumptions: The theory operates in the weak-disorder limit and utilizes semiclassical approximations, including the small-momentum-transfer approximation for scattering calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the four disorder-induced contributions to the OEE, while Figure 2 decomposes the total orbital magnetization into five distinct components based on scattering mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper builds from a general semiclassical Boltzmann framework, decomposing the collision integral into multiple scattering channels. It then analyzes the symmetry properties of these channels, culminating in quantitative results for the orbital magnetization in the Rashba 2DEG.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous symmetry analysis (T-odd vs. T-even contributions) and the explicit separation of scattering mechanisms provide a powerful theoretical template for analyzing non-equilibrium phenomena in quantum systems.
